content: Probabilistic forecast validation: (1) Empirical coverage check: for a nominal 95% PI, the actual fraction of test observations within the interval should be ~0.95. Systematic deviation = miscalibration (over-confident if coverage < nominal, under-confident if coverage > nominal). (2) MSIS (Scaled Interval Score): scores both sharpness and coverage jointly, proper scoring rule, lower is better, scaled by naive baseline for cross-series comparison. (3) Pinball loss / quantile score: at quantile tau, penalizes under-predictions by (1-tau)*|e| and over-predictions by tau*|e|; proper scoring rule for individual quantiles. (4) CRPS: integral of pinball loss across all quantiles 0..1; evaluates full predictive distribution; proper scoring rule. (5) For conformal prediction specifically: validate marginal coverage (average across test points) with chi-squared or binomial test against nominal alpha; conditional coverage (per subgroup) requires larger samples. (6) For Gaussian outputs: test calibration via PIT histogram — if forecasts are calibrated, the probability integral transform U(F(Y),0,1) should be uniform.
